PullRequest.Title: sessions: keep list selection on the open chat after a move
PullRequest.Body:
Fixes #345631

After a chat move (drag, Move to Session…, Move to New Session, reorder), the sessions list revealed the moved row and **selected** it without opening it, so the list selection and the open chat disagreed.

**Cause:** `revealMoved` in `sessionsList.ts` called `tree.setSelection([element])`. In this list selection means "the open chat" (`syncActiveChatSelection` / `onDidOpen`), so selecting without opening broke the invariant. Likely regression from #344929 (not bisected).

**Fix:** `revealMoved` still reveals and focuses the moved row; it selects it only when it is the open chat (so the selection follows the open chat to where it went).

**Tests**
- Red on unfixed code (4+ failures incl. the new stays-on-open-chat test), green after: `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"` → 9752 passing.
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run eslint <changed files>` pass.
- New tests: selection stays on the open chat while the moved row is revealed+focused; moved chat that is the open chat stays selected.

**Live check** (Code - OSS, throwaway profile, mock host + Copilot chats): with chat A open, dragging B onto C nests B; A stays open and selected, B is revealed and focused (`selected: [A]`, `focused: [B]`). Not covered live: moving the open chat itself (unit-covered only), and a before-fix live run (red unit run used instead).

Scenarios.Scenario: A user drags or commands a chat/session move, including reordering within a session, moving into another session, or creating a new session.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing move command awaits the provider operation; the provider catalog event/list update must then expose the destination row before reveal/focus completes. The diff adds only in-memory observable reads and a URI equality check after the row is found, before an optional selection update.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Move a chat or session through the agent-host connection (`connection.moveChat` or `connection.moveSession`).
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one provider/agent-host call per accepted user move; no per-row or per-chat fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single provider call and catalog/list update were required before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing boundary is awaited before the command reports success; catalog propagation then drives destination-row discovery. The added active-chat check occurs afterward and does not delay or multiply the boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One logical move at a time is watched; pendingMoveReveal replaces the previous watcher. A successful reveal executes the new check once, independent of session/chat collection size. Existing row lookup and list rendering behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One provider move promise per user action. Move-reveal tracking retains only the latest move and retries on at most five list updates; the added check runs only on the successful reveal, not on failed retries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider uses its existing cached session/chat catalog to resolve source, destination, and anchors. The new active-session and active-chat reads are warm in-memory observables, add no cache key or miss behavior, and do not invalidate or populate caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the call path shows the changed code runs only after destination resolution and performs two observable reads plus URI comparison; all expensive provider work is pre-existing.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency and catalog propagation vary by local versus remote host, but the diff neither adds nor reschedules those operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. For background-chat moves the diff removes `setSelection`; for open-chat moves it preserves that update after constant-time in-memory identity checks.

Scenarios.Scenario: The open chat itself is moved, or a different chat is moved while another chat remains open, and the sessions list reconciles focus and selection.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the moved row becomes visible, reveal and focus remain synchronous UI work. The diff reads the active session/chat and calls `setSelection` only when the row represents that open chat; active-session changes also continue to use the pre-existing next-animation-frame list update path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One check per successfully revealed move and at most one selected row. Cost does not grow with history, number of rendered rows, or move retries.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous on the successful reveal callback; active-session rendering remains coalesced by the existing `MutableDisposable` animation-frame schedule. No new queue, burst, or listener is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Active session/chat values are held by observables and read directly. There is no cold path, negative cache, persistence access, or coalescing change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: `isOpenChat` performs only observable reads and URI equality, and the changed branch can only suppress the prior selection call.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact DOM cost of `setSelection` depends on list state, but the diff executes it no more often than before and skips it for non-open rows.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression; synchronous UI work is reduced or unchanged, and no rendering/layout loop or collection-wide work was added.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the full three-file diff and traced the move/reveal path through list scheduling and agent-host provider boundaries. The production change adds a constant-time active-chat identity check once per successful move reveal and conditionally avoids an existing selection update. Tests and harness changes do not affect product runtime. No actionable performance issue or concrete performance-regression fix was found.
